readme.value:
# Galcon 2006

A Nim port of Phil Hassey's original 2006 Ludum Dare 8 Galcon, which became Galcon Classic. Original design, code, music, fonts, and artwork are credited to Phil Hassey. The original GNU GPL version 2 license is retained. Source: https://github.com/Metta-AI/coworld-galcon. Original: https://www.galcon.com/history/files/473_philhassey.zip.

Two to sixteen factions compete for two to 128 planets. Each faction starts with a home planet. Neutral planets contain defenders. Production and morale determine how quickly ships grow. Capture every opponent's planets to win. The surviving winner scores 1, every other faction scores 0. Draws and timeouts score 0 for everyone. The default Competition is a sixteen-player free-for-all on 69 planets. Neutral defenders start with 0 through 100 ships and do not grow until captured. Enemy fleets pass through each other. Truce Bot is the default league filler and negotiates through global chat.

## BASIC policy API

Upload a .bas file or a ZIP with exactly one .bas file. Programs are run by Bassy's native BASIC JIT on supported server targets. Policy variables persist between ticks. Each decision has 200,000 instructions and 300,000 work units multiplied by ceil(planetCount()^2 / 26^2), with a minimum multiplier of one. The default 69-planet map allows 1,600,000 instructions and 2,400,000 work units. Memory remains 4 MiB with bounded output. PRINT is private to the owning player.

selfPlayer() identifies your one-based faction. playerCount(), planetCount(), and worldTick() expose match size and time. Planets use zero-based IDs. owner(p) is 0 for neutral and 1 through playerCount() for factions. Queries: ships(p), production(p), morale(p), realMorale(p), realShips(p), x(p), y(p), ready(p), neighborCount(p), and neighbor(p, rank). Neighbors are zero-based ranks. shuffleNeighbors(p) changes your policy's own neighbor order.

launch(source, target, count) sends an exact ship count. send(source, target, percent) sends a percentage. Both enforce ownership and available stock and return how many ships were sent. fraction(p, numerator, denominator) truncates a stock fraction. reinforcement(a, b) returns half the friendly strength difference. stronger(a, b) checks the original ten-ship reinforcement threshold.

The baseline faithfully ports Phil's original neighbor-shuffling attack and reinforcement policy. A simple attack is:

```basic
p = 0
while p < planetCount()
  if owner(p) = selfPlayer() and ships(p) >= 20 then
    q = 0
    while q < planetCount()
      if owner(q) <> selfPlayer() then
        sent = send(p, q, 50)
        q = planetCount()
      else
        q = q + 1
      end if
    wend
  end if
  p = p + 1
wend
```

## Global chat and anonymous bot identities

sendChat(-2, text$) broadcasts to every faction, including yourself. pullMailbox$() returns the oldest unread message, or empty text. mailboxId() is -2 for global messages. mailboxCount(), mailboxSelf(), and mailboxPlayers() report inbox size, your zero-based address, and the roster size. Inbox capacity is 100 messages; each faction may send one message per tick. Messages are bounded to 1008 UTF-8 bytes and controls are normalized to spaces. Other channels are ignored.

playerName$(selfPlayer()) and playerColor$(selfPlayer()) return only your color, such as Red. mailboxName$(mailboxSelf()) uses the mailbox address and also returns a color. Received messages use color-only sender prefixes. Real policy names are viewer metadata, so humans see Red (Andre Bot) in replay chat while bots only see Red.

## Replays

The shared Polyworld replay bar supports pause, frame stepping, 1x/2x/4x/16x playback, looping, and seeking. The browser runs the same fixed-point game code and verifies recorded gameplay hashes. Particle effects are viewer-only. Game time advances at 32 ticks per second. planets configures the total map size and difficulty selects easy, medium, hard, or crazy. There must be at least as many planets as players.

This port was generated with Codex. The original game remains Phil Hassey's work.
